1.name: Martial Arts
1.notes:
Your training grants you mastery of unarmed combat and certain weapons. Your Monk weapons are Simple melee weapons and Martial melee weapons with the Light property.

While you are unarmored, not wielding a Shield, and wielding only Monk weapons (or no weapons), you gain the following benefits:
• Bonus Unarmed Strike. You can make one Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action.
• Martial Arts Die. You can use a d6 in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons; this die increases as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the class table.
• Dexterous Attacks. You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons. When you use your Unarmed Strike to Grapple or Shove, you can use Dexterity instead of Strength to determine the save DC.

1.name: Unarmored Defense
1.notes: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

2.name: Monk’s Focus
2.notes:
You gain a pool of Focus Points that fuels certain Monk features. The number of points is shown in the class table. You regain all expended Focus Points when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Some features that use Focus Points require a saving throw; the DC equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

You start knowing the following options:
• Flurry of Blows. You can spend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action.
• Patient Defense. You can take the Disengage action as a Bonus Action. Alternatively, you can spend 1 Focus Point to take both the Disengage and Dodge actions as a Bonus Action.
• Step of the Wind. You can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action. Alternatively, you can spend 1 Focus Point to take both the Disengage and Dash actions as a Bonus Action, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

2.name: Unarmored Movement
2.notes: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your Speed increases by 10 feet. This bonus increases at higher Monk levels, as shown in the class table.

2.name: Uncanny Metabolism
2.notes:
When you roll Initiative, you can instantly regain all expended Focus Points. When you do, roll your Martial Arts die and regain Hit Points equal to your Monk level + the number rolled.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

3.name: Deflect Attacks
3.notes:
When a creature hits you with an attack that deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can use a Reaction to reduce the total damage to you by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can spend 1 Focus Point to redirect the attack. Choose a creature you can see: within 5 feet of you if the original attack was melee, or within 60 feet and not behind Total Cover if it was ranged. That creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die + your Dexterity modifier, of the same type as the original attack.

3.name: Subclass Feature
3.notes: You choose a Monk subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Monk levels.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at levels 8, 12, and 16.

4.name: Slow Fall
4.notes: When you fall, you can use a Reaction to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.notes: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

5.name: Stunning Strike
5.notes:
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can spend 1 Focus Point to attempt to stun it. The target must make a Constitution saving throw.
On a failed save, it is Stunned until the start of your next turn.
On a successful save, its Speed is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against it before then has Advantage.

6.name: Empowered Strikes
6.notes: Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, you can choose for the damage to be Force instead of its normal type.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.notes: You gain a level 6 feature from your Monk subclass.

7.name: Evasion
7.notes:
When an effect allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage on a successful save and only half damage on a failed save.
You don’t benefit from this feature if you are Incapacitated.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

9.name: Acrobatic Movement
9.notes: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you can move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.

10.name: Heightened Focus
10.notes:
Your Focus options improve:

• Flurry of Blows. When you spend 1 Focus Point to use Flurry of Blows, you make three Unarmed Strikes instead of two.

• Patient Defense. When you spend 1 Focus Point to use Patient Defense, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.

• Step of the Wind. When you spend 1 Focus Point to use Step of the Wind, you can choose a willing creature within 5 feet of you that is Large or smaller. That creature moves with you until the end of your turn, and this movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks for the creature.

10.name: Self-Restoration
10.notes:
At the end of each of your turns, you can end one of the following conditions on yourself: Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned.
In addition, you no longer suffer Exhaustion from going without food or drink.

11.name: Subclass Feature
11.notes: You gain a level 11 feature from your Monk subclass.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

13.name: Deflect Energy
13.notes: You can now apply your Deflect Attacks feature to attacks that deal any damage type, not only Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

14.name: Disciplined Survivor
14.notes:
You gain proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, when you fail a saving throw, you can spend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.

15.name: Perfect Focus
15.notes: When you roll Initiative and choose not to use Uncanny Metabolism, you automatically regain Focus Points until you have 4, if you currently have 3 or fewer.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

17.name: Subclass Feature
17.notes: You gain a level 17 feature from your Monk subclass.

18.name: Superior Defense
18.notes: At the start of your turn, you can spend 3 Focus Points to harden your defenses for 1 minute or until you are Incapacitated. For the duration, you have Resistance to all damage except Force.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.notes: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Irresistible Offense is recommended.

20.name: Body and Mind
20.notes: You have perfected your physical and mental discipline. Your Dexterity score increases by 4, and your Wisdom score increases by 4, to a maximum of 25 for each.
